taxonomy.subtopic: CD40 ligand-dependent class switching and germinal-center formation

questions.stem_html: A 10-month-old boy has recurrent bacterial respiratory infections and Pneumocystis pneumonia. Serum IgM is elevated, whereas IgG, IgA, and IgE are markedly decreased. Lymph-node biopsy shows poorly developed germinal centers. The accompanying diagram shows an activated helper T cell failing to deliver a signal to a B cell. Which T-cell molecule is most likely absent?
questions.explanation_html: Activated helper T cells express CD40 ligand, which binds CD40 on B cells and is required for germinal-center formation, immunoglobulin class switching, affinity maturation, and memory formation. X-linked CD40 ligand deficiency therefore produces normal or elevated IgM with low IgG, IgA, and IgE and also impairs macrophage activation, increasing susceptibility to opportunistic infections.

wrong_choice_explanations.2: CD28 provides costimulation to T cells by binding B7 molecules on antigen-presenting cells; its absence does not selectively block B-cell class switching with elevated IgM.
wrong_choice_explanations.3: CTLA-4 is an inhibitory receptor that limits T-cell activation rather than delivering the class-switch signal to B cells.
wrong_choice_explanations.4: Fas ligand participates in activation-induced cell death and cytotoxic pathways; it is not the key signal for immunoglobulin isotype switching.
wrong_choice_explanations.5: The interleukin-2 receptor alpha chain supports lymphocyte proliferation but does not directly mediate CD40-dependent class switching.

questions.educational_objective: CD40 ligand on activated helper T cells is required for B-cell class switching, germinal-center formation, affinity maturation, and effective macrophage activation.
